"The search for an Indian tourist who fell into a sinkhole in Kuala Lumpur has been suspended due to safety concerns. Vijaya Lakshmi Gali was walking on a road in Malaysia's capital on August 23rd when the pavement suddenly collapsed beneath her, causing her to plunge into an 8-meter-deep sinkhole and vanish from sight.

***

Rescue teams have conducted an extensive search operation spanning eight days, utilizing tracker dogs, remote cameras, and ground-penetrating radar technology. Despite these comprehensive efforts, searchers have discovered no trace of the missing woman except for her slippers that were left behind at the scene.

***

Malaysia's fire and rescue department declared the search too dangerous to continue, particularly citing risks to diving personnel. Two divers attempted to enter the sinkhole on Thursday but were quickly withdrawn before reaching any obstacles due to hazardous conditions underground.

***

* Authorities employed high-pressure water jets and excavators to flush portions of the underground drainage system and remove debris during the rescue operation.

***

Dr Zaliha Mustafa, a minister in the prime minister's department, explained that multiple factors contributed to halting the operation, with the safety and health of rescue personnel being the primary concern. Officials also noted that a soil slip had occurred in the same location the previous year. Is there anything else I can help with?"
